title: Summit Earning Rates by Tier
content:
In the Crestline Summit Loyalty Program the tier a member holds sets two earning rates: the award miles earned for each US dollar of eligible fare on a flown Crestline coupon, and the elite bonus earned on partner airline flights, expressed as a percent of the partner's base miles.

| Tier | Award miles per USD of eligible fare on a flown Crestline coupon | Elite bonus on partner airline flights (percent of the partner's base miles) |
|---|---|---|
| Summit Member | 5 | 0 |
| Summit Silver | 7 | 25 |
| Summit Gold | 8 | 40 |
| Summit Platinum | 9 | 50 |
| Summit Diamond | 11 | 100 |
| Summit Chairman | 11 | 120 |

**Notes to the table**

1. The first column is a rate per whole US dollar of eligible fare, the eligible fare being the base fare share of the segment excluding government taxes.
2. The second column applies to partner airline activity only; it is a percent of the base miles the partner reports.
3. Summit Diamond and Summit Chairman share the same award-mile rate, 11 per USD; they differ in the partner airline bonus, 100 percent against 120 percent.

**Hypothetical reading.** On an eligible fare of 200 USD, the rate column gives 1000 award miles at the Summit Member rate of 5 and 1800 award miles at the Summit Platinum rate of 9, before any rounding or addition the earning rules set. On a partner airline flight reported at 2000 base miles, the Summit Gold bonus of 40 percent is 800 miles.
